page: Amazon Web Services m6g.12xlarge is a general-purpose cloud server powered by 64-bit Arm-based AWS Graviton processors with ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 48 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with one thread per core. Memory capacity totals 192.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Cache hierarchy consists of 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and 32 MB shared L3 cache. There is no bundled local storage included, requiring reliance on remote EBS volumes, while the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded scaling alongside moderate single-thread compute. In stress-ng testing, multi-core throughput scored 72,816.53, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested systems, whereas single-core stress-ng settled in the middle 50 percent at 1,519.38. Similarly, Geekbench single-core scored 961.0 in the bottom 25 percent, while multi-core achieved 12,988.0. In memory throughput, read performance on 256 MB blocks hit 172.16 GB/sec and write performance reached 79.95 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 58.52 million Redis SET operations per second and 41.42 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

The physical core dedication eliminates hyperthreading resource contention, offering consistent thread performance for containerized environments and microservices. However, the lack of local NVMe storage limits low-latency scratch disk workflows, and modest single-core execution makes it less suitable for unparallelized tasks or real-time text generation on large language models. The instance offers resource balance and efficient multi-core density, fitting scale-out web serving, caching tiers, compilation tasks, and multi-threaded business applications.
description: Amazon Web Services m6g.12xlarge is an Arm-based general-purpose instance featuring 48 dedicated Graviton Neoverse-N1 cores operating at 2.5 GHz and 192.0 GB of system memory. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per physical core alongside a 20 Gbps network baseline. The server contains no integrated local storage and features zero GPUs. Performance benchmarks show upper-quartile multi-core compute in stress-ng tests (72,816.53), paired with average memory bandwidth and 58.52 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads. Single-thread execution is modest, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 961.0. The configuration delivers consistent resource isolation across parallel threads, making it suitable for container orchestration, multi-threaded backend services, distributed caching, and static web serving.
